coverage.assessment: Three bridges are weak or missing: the bridge from Pteraspis to the law-school method, from 'talk' to the half-a-dozen limit, and from King's achievements to 'richest'. The model setup before King survives but has lost its 'better system' motive.

Rooms, Brooks above and Dennett opposite, Hague's party, the mule, the cabin, King's arrival and the shared bed are all clear. 'The standard' in p2 is slightly vaguer after 'primitive arrangements' was cut, but still readable.
The only performed speech, the Chicago answer, is exact and attributed to one student in reply to Adams's question.
Two hedges are lost: 'So far as it went, the answer was good' and 'They might perhaps be frauds'. Seven-year and 1877 anticipations are correctly framed.
Retrospective items are cast as anticipation. King's prediction stands without any hint of failure, and nothing anticipates later private events.
Several aphoristic closers and King's cumulative portrait are cut. The triads, semicolon chains and closing punchlines that survive still carry the voice.
The two-way contrast between King's straight line and Adams's breaks survives. The east/west convergence image and the 'better system' frame are thinned.
The Pteraspis, prediction, and Lyell dependencies are intact at both endpoints in this run's drafts.

strengths: All eight verbatim passages survive exactly, including the parent/murderer/teacher triad and the closing 'Henceforth, he went on, submissive.'
Retrospective spans are consistently reframed as anticipation ('lay before him', 'was to quit', 'was to write nothing'), satisfying the continuity check.
The Estes Park sequence keeps the comic beats ('the fish moved eastward', 'allowed he was lost', mule cleverer than himself) and the full cabin and shared-bed scene with King.
The childhood drawing-room memory paired with renting the same room, with Brooks above and Dennett opposite, is preserved intact.
summary: The revision is close to the 2,900-word target. It keeps all eight verbatim passages, the continuity checks (seven years framed as anticipation, Brooks, Emmons, Greeley buggy, thirty-three), and all three planned dependencies. There are no blockers. To reach the target, though, it cuts several connective and qualifying sentences. These include the hinge into the law-school method, the ironic acceptance of the Chicago answer, the build-up of King's portrait, and the concrete basis for King's 'great success' and 'richest'. The 'better system' motive that frames King as model is also gone. Most repairs are short sentence restorations that can be offset by trimming elsewhere.
